name: Benzinga
description: Real-time financial newswire and analyst coverage for US-listed companies: market-moving headlines, why-is-it-moving notes, press releases, ratings changes and consensus, announced deals, and unusual options activity.

tools.name: Consensus ratings
tools.description: Use for where analysts stand in aggregate right now on one company. For the individual changes that moved the consensus, use calendar/ratings instead.

options.about: Exactly one ticker symbol to aggregate for; the endpoint takes a single ticker, not a list. Call once per company.
options.name: parameters[tickers]

options.about: Earliest date, YYYY-MM-DD.
options.name: parameters[date_from]

options.about: Latest date, YYYY-MM-DD.
options.name: parameters[date_to]

options.about: Collapse the aggregate to BUY, HOLD and SELL rather than the five-step scale.
options.name: simplify

options.about: Whether each rating bucket is reported as a count of analysts or as a percentage of them.
options.name: aggregate_type

options.about: Records to return. Limit 1000.
options.name: pagesize

response.about: The analyst consensus for a ticker as counts per rating bucket, plus consensus price targets. Note this endpoint sits outside the calendar family and takes no page parameter.

tools.name: Analyst ratings

options.about: Comma-separated response fields to return, or * for every field including ratings_accuracy. Available: id, date, time, ticker, exchange, name, currency, action_pt, action_company, rating_current, pt_current, rating_prior, pt_prior, pt_pct_change, url, url_calendar, url_news, analyst, analyst_id, analyst_name, firm_id, ratings_accuracy, importance, notes, updated. Set it to trim the payload when you only need the rating and target.

tools.name: Analyst roster
tools.description: Use to resolve an analyst by name, or to judge how accurate a particular analyst has been, and to get the id you then pass to calendar/ratings as parameters[analyst_id]. For the ratings themselves use calendar/ratings; for the list of firms rather than people use calendar/ratings-firms.

options.about: Page offset, limited to 0-100000. Set this only when walking past the first page of the analyst roster.
options.name: page

options.about: Number of analysts to return, limit 1000. Raise it when you want the roster in one call rather than paging.
options.name: pageSize

options.about: Comma-separated list of response fields to return. Set it to trim the payload when you only need names and ids and not the ratings_accuracy block.
options.name: fields

options.about: Analyst identifier to look up. Set this when you already have an analyst_id from a ratings record and want that analyst's profile and accuracy.
options.name: analyst

options.about: Analyst name to match. Set this when the caller names a person rather than supplying an id; the reference does not say whether matching is exact, so try the full name first.
options.name: analyst_name

options.about: Firm identifier to restrict to. Set this to list only the analysts working at one research firm.
options.name: firm

options.about: Firm name to match. Use it when the caller names the bank, for example Morgan Stanley, instead of supplying a firm id.
options.name: firm_name

options.about: Unix timestamp (UTC); only records updated at or after this are returned, and the sort order follows it. Set this to poll for roster changes since your last sync.
options.name: updated

response.about: The roster of analysts who issue ratings, each with their firm and, when present, a rank and ratings_accuracy block of historical hit rates. The docs list the top-level fields; the rank and ratings_accuracy objects are nested and their child attributes are collapsed in the reference.

fields.about: Benzinga analyst id, the value to pass as parameters[analyst_id] when filtering ratings.
fields.name: id

fields.about: Analyst's full name.
fields.name: name_full

fields.about: Analyst's first name.
fields.name: name_first

fields.about: Analyst's last name.
fields.name: name_last

fields.about: Id of the firm the analyst works for.
fields.name: firm_id

fields.about: Name of the firm the analyst works for.
fields.name: firm_name

fields.about: Ranking object for the analyst; child attributes are not enumerated in the docs.
fields.name: rank

fields.about: Historical accuracy block with success rates, average returns, smart scores and total ratings over 1m, 3m, 9m, 1y, 2y, 3y and overall windows.
fields.name: ratings_accuracy

fields.about: Unix timestamp of the last update to this analyst record.
fields.name: updated

tools.name: Research firms
tools.description: Use to enumerate the covering firms or to turn a firm name into the id that calendar/ratings filters on as parameters[firm_id]. For an individual analyst and their track record use calendar/ratings-analysts; for the ratings themselves use calendar/ratings.

options.about: Page offset, limited to 0-100000. Set this only when paging past the first block of firms.
options.name: page

options.about: Number of firms to return, limit 1000. Raise it to pull the whole firm list in one call.
options.name: pageSize

options.about: Comma-separated list of response fields to return. Set it when you only need id and name.
options.name: fields

options.about: Firm identifier to look up. Set this when you already hold a firm_id from a ratings record and want the firm's details.
options.name: firm

options.about: Unix timestamp (UTC); only firms updated at or after this are returned. Set this to poll for newly added or renamed firms since your last sync.
options.name: updated

response.about: The research firms that publish analyst ratings. The sample payload carries only id and name per firm; the reference additionally documents currency, homepage and updated.

fields.about: Benzinga firm id, the value to pass as parameters[firm_id] when filtering ratings.
fields.name: id

fields.about: Firm name as Benzinga records it.
fields.name: name

fields.name: currency

fields.about: Firm's website.
fields.name: homepage

fields.about: Unix timestamp of the last update to this firm record.
fields.name: updated

tools.name: Removed calendar events
tools.description: Use when you keep a copy of the ratings or M&A calendar and need to know which previously returned events have since been withdrawn, which Schedule C.10 requires you to act on. It answers only what disappeared; for the events themselves use calendar/ratings or calendar/mergers-acquisitions.

options.about: Page offset, limited to 0-100000. Set this when walking a long backlog of removals.
options.name: page

options.about: Number of removal records to return, limit 1000.
options.name: pageSize

options.about: Which calendar to read removals for: ratings for calendar/ratings rows, ma for calendar/mergers-acquisitions rows. Always set it: left unset the feed returns removals from every Benzinga calendar, most of them for calendars not published here (probed 2026-09-21, the unfiltered first page was dividends).
options.name: type

options.about: Unix timestamp (UTC); only records updated at or after this are returned. Set this to the time of your last sync so you get just the newly withdrawn events.
options.name: updated

response.about: Calendar events Benzinga has removed or cancelled, identified by id and the calendar they came from, so you can delete matching rows from a copy you hold.

fields.about: Id of the removed event; match it against the id you stored from calendar/ratings or calendar/mergers-acquisitions.
fields.name: id

fields.about: Which calendar the removed event belonged to, ratings or ma.
fields.name: type

fields.about: Unix timestamp of the removal record.
fields.name: updated

tools.name: Press releases
tools.description: Use this for company-issued announcements distributed over the wires, the primary-source wording behind a story. For Benzinga editorial coverage and the wider newswire use news/search, and for the one-line explanation of a price move use news/wiims.

options.name: pageSize

options.name: displayOutput

options.about: A single day to query, yyyy-mm-dd. Use it instead of dateFrom and dateTo when the caller names one date.

options.name: dateFrom

options.about: Unix timestamp in UTC; set it to your last sync time to pull only releases updated since then.

options.about: Sort order as field:direction. Use created:asc to read a period forwards, or updated:desc when tracking edits.
options.name: sort

options.about: Comma-separated CUSIPs, maximum 50; requires a license agreement. Use only when the caller supplies CUSIPs.

options.about: Comma-separated ticker symbols, maximum 50. Set this whenever the caller names a company.

options.name: primaryTickers

options.about: Comma-separated words or phrases matched against title, tags and body in that order of priority. Use it when the caller asks about a subject rather than a company.

options.about: Comma-separated authors, which for press releases are the distributing wires. Set it to restrict to one wire.

options.about: Desired response format. Set text only when you want plain text rather than the default JSON structures.

options.about: Importance level of the release. Set high when the caller only wants the market-moving releases.

options.about: Region filter, for example 'ca' or 'canada' for Canadian content. Set it when the caller scopes the question to a market.
options.name: region
